article.title: Second Conditional
article.description: Structure: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. Used for hypothetical or unlikely present/future situations: 'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.' Common mistake: using 'would' in the if-clause too — 'If I would win the lottery' is incorrect; the if-clause always uses past simple.
article.content: Structure: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. Used for hypothetical or unlikely present/future situations: 'If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.' Common mistake: using 'would' in the if-clause too — 'If I would win the lottery' is incorrect; the if-clause always uses past simple.

generated.caption:
Ever imagine what you'd do if something unlikely happened? 🤔 That's the Second Conditional!

We use 'If + past simple, ... would + base verb' for hypothetical present or future situations. For example: "If I won the lottery, I would travel the world."

Remember, the 'if' clause always uses past simple, never 'would'!

generated.script: If I would win the lottery... ye sunne mein theek lagta hai na? Par English grammar mein ye ek common mistake hai! Toh, baat ho rahi hai Second Conditional ki. Isko hum use karte hain jab hum kisi hypothetical ya unlikely present ya future situation ke baare mein baat kar rahe hote hain. Iska structure hai: If + past simple, then... would + base verb. For example: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. Yahan won past simple hai. Common mistake kya hai? If-clause mein would laga dena. Jaise, If I would win... ye galat hai. If-clause mein always past simple use hota hai, would kabhi nahi. Ab samajh aaya? So, next time, agar aap kisi hypothetical situation ki baat kar rahe ho, always use If + past simple. If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. Toh, comment mein batao, aapko ye rule pata tha ya nahi! Aur aise hi English tips ke liye follow karo The English Vault!

slides.headlineRest: — Master Hypothetical Situations & Avoid Common Mistakes
slides.body: The Second Conditional is used to talk about hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future. Its structure is "If + past simple, ... would + base verb." For example, "If I won the lottery, I would travel the world." A common mistake is using 'would' in the 'if' clause, like "If I would win the lottery," which is incorrect. Remember, the 'if' clause always uses the past simple tense, never 'would'.
